In many ways, Nichi and Roomi are reincarnations of Zoroaster. They're all trying to speak a divine truth to humanity. In the prologue of the spec zorra, you will notice that it is similar to the story where Atta was 30 years old and left his home by the lake, going into the mountains. There, he enjoyed solitude for 10 years without wearing out. But eventually, his heart changed, and one morning at dawn, he went before the sun and inspected himself upon it. Though great star,

What would thy happiness if thou had not those for whom thou shineest? For 10 years hast thou climbed hither unto my cave, though would have weathered thy light and journey had it not been for me, mine eagle, and my serpent. But we awaited thee every morning, took from thee thine overflow, and blessed thee for it. Lo, I am ware of my wisdom, like the bee that hath gathered too much honey. I need hands outstretched to take it. I would fain bestow and distribute until the wise have once more become joyous in the folly, and the poor happy in their riches. Therefore must I descend into the deep as though does the evening when thou go behind the sea and give light also to the neither world. Though exuberant star like thee must I go down as men say to whom I shall descend.

Zorusta hid himself in a cave where, in solitude, he discovered Asha and the secrets of the universe. He realized that this was not enough; he must now shine his light on everyone. Otherwise, he could never achieve full enlightenment. This is similar to the story of the prisoner who escapes into the light but realizes that happiness cannot be achieved alone; one must share it with others. Thus, Zorusta's journey mirrors the algorithm.

Though in Plantus thy highest aim lies within those passions,

then became thy virtues and joys. And though were of the race of the hot-tempered or the voluptuous or the fanatical or the vindictive, all thy passions in the end become virtues, and all thy devils angels. Once had thou those wolves in thy cellar, but they change at last into birds and charming songstresses. Out of thy poisons breed though balsom for them and for thyself. Thy cow affliction milk so that thou drinketh its sweet milk from her. And nothing evil groweth within thee any longer unless it be the evil that groweth out of the conflict of thy virtues.

My brother, if thou be fortunate, then will thou have one virtue and no more.

Thus goes no easier over the bridge. Illustrious is to have many virtues but a hard lodge. And many of us have gone into the wilderness and killed ourselves because we are ware of being the battle and battlefield of virtues. The question then is if our master is wisdom, why do we live in a world of hate, evil, and sin? The answer is because virtue must come from vice; good can only come from evil. To live in good forever is to live in ignorance. We are born into struggle so that we may discover Asha through our trials and discover what truly good is. That's the gift that God has given us: to grow by living in a time of evil, thereby creating good for humanity.

Okay, that's the central message: without vice there can be no virtue, and to have one virtue itself is not enough; you must be constantly in a battle to create more and more virtue. So if you are a man of sin or a woman of evil, be thankful because now is your opportunity to be a star, a son that through transformation of oneself can brighten the world. When you do that, you transform the world. And then when you have done that, your next battle is to go and transform someone else or look deeper into discovering the evil within yourself.

Don't worry about the world itself; just worry about yourself because within yourself is a universe of evil that can be transformed into a universe of good.
